clinician.final_diagnosis: Fatal invasive osteomyelitis in an allo-HSCT recipient caused by RM (Rhizomucor)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old male with newly diagnosed MDS RAEB-I (complex karyotype) underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation 6 months prior to presentation. He presented to the emergency department with critical sepsis (fever >40°C, dyspnea, respiratory failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation). CT imaging showed bilateral pulmonary infiltrations. Initial microbiologic investigations (blood cultures and bronchoalveolar lavage) were negative for bacterial, viral, or fungal organisms. The patient was treated with empiric antibiotic, antiviral (acyclovir), and antifungal (azole) therapy. After respiratory stabilization, the patient developed right hip pain. Imaging (ultrasound, CT, and MRI) of the right hip revealed multiple old bone infarcts in both femurs and a new infarct with massive secondary osteomyelitis in the right femoral head, neck, and trochanteric region with breakthrough into surrounding soft tissue. Emergency surgical intervention revealed extensive bone and soft tissue destruction with characteristic blackened tissue. Proximal femoral resection with vancomycin, gentamycin, clindamycin, and amphotericin B-loaded spacer placement and extensive tissue debridement were performed. Microbiological and histopathological analysis with BLAST identified RM (Rhizomucor) from the surgical specimen. Six weeks after re-admission, whole-body MRI revealed multiple additional bone infarctions (left femur, both humeri, both tibiae) with suspected superinfection of RM, indicating disseminated mucormycosis. The patient had a fatal outcome from this invasive mucormycosis infection.
